description: Verify that an ARP cache entry ages out when idle — after <DYNAMIC-ARP-CACHE-TIMEOUT> seconds without use, DUT must re-resolve via a fresh ARP Request before its next UDP egress
approach:
[Objective]
Idle aging keeps stale mappings from accumulating. DUT first uses a learned entry (proves it was cached), then waits past the cache-timeout, then is asked to send to the same IP again — at which point it must NOT reuse the now-expired entry but must re-ARP.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: ARP Request injected (sender_ip=HOST-1-IP, sender_mac=MAC-ADDR1) → DUT learns.

2. Tester → DUT: SOME/IP SubscribeEventgroup
   ⇒ DUT sends UDP #1 to HOST-1-IP, eth_dst should be MAC-ADDR1 (learned).

3. Idle wait of <DYNAMIC-ARP-CACHE-TIMEOUT> seconds (no traffic) — entry must age out.

4. Tester → DUT: SOME/IP SubscribeEventgroup
   ⇒ DUT must resolve again. Observe DUT's own ARP Request for HOST-1-IP.

[Pass condition]
UDP #1 used MAC-ADDR1, then post-timeout an ARP Request from DUT for HOST-1-IP is observed.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_udp1_wrong_eth_dst — UDP #1 didn't use MAC-ADDR1 (initial learning broken)
• Fail_no_udp1 — UDP #1 absent (initial trigger broken)
• Fail_no_arp_request_after_timeout — DUT did not re-ARP after the idle period (entry did not age out)

verdicts.Pass: DUT used learned entry then re-ARPed after timeout — normal aging
verdicts.Fail_udp1_wrong_eth_dst: Initial UDP did not use the learned MAC — initial learning broken
verdicts.Fail_no_udp1: Initial UDP not observed — first stimulus did not trigger egress
verdicts.Fail_no_arp_request_after_timeout: DUT did not re-ARP after the idle wait — cache entry did not expire
